_about: A verse, a saint quote and a reflection question for each day of the year (from the maintainer’s own catholic-daily-reflection project). Verse references are Douay-Rheims/Vulgate numbering; the text shown is read from the reader’s own translation. Saint quotes are shown as attributed: only those found word for word in this app’s library texts are marked verified.

saint.text: You have made us for Yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in You.

entries.question: As you begin this new year, what specific restlessness in your heart are you asking God to fill?

saint.text: A tree is known by its fruit; a man by his deeds. A good deed is never lost.

entries.question: Looking at the 'fruit' of your recent actions, would others recognize the wisdom of God in them?

saint.text: The Name of Jesus is the glory of preachers, because the shining splendor of that Name causes his word to be proclaimed and heard.

entries.question: How can you speak the name of Jesus with more reverence in your conversations today?

saint.text: The first end I propose in our daily work is to do the will of God.

entries.question: Is your current 'delight' found in following your own will or seeking God's?

saint.text: We must love our neighbor as being made in the image of God and as an object of His love.

entries.question: How does seeing your neighbor as an 'image of God' change the way you treat them?

entries.question: What 'star' or sign is God currently using to lead you closer to Him?

entries.question: Which of your own 'prudent' plans are you most afraid to surrender to God's will?

saint.text: Prayer is the wings by which the soul flies to God.

entries.question: What 'gift' from today can you trace back to God's providence rather than your own hard work?

saint.text: Knowledge without love only puffeth up; but love edifieth.

entries.question: Are you using your intelligence to serve others, or to make yourself feel superior?

saint.text: A soul that loves God finds its peace even in the midst of trials.

entries.question: Is your peace currently dependent on your circumstances, or on your union with Christ?

saint.text: We should use the things of this world as if we used them not.

entries.question: If everything you owned was taken away today, would your identity in Christ remain unshaken?

saint.text: Faith is the foundation of all that we do.

entries.question: Has your charity 'increased' toward the person you find most difficult to be around?

saint.text: True nobility is found in the service of God.

entries.question: Are your words today building up (edifying) those around you, or are they tearing them down?

saint.text: Humility is the only ladder that reaches to heaven.

entries.question: In what way is God being a 'shield' for you today by closing a door that was dangerous for your soul?

saint.text: Mary offered herself to God in the temple, and so should we.

entries.question: How can you 'present' your daily work to God today as a holy offering?

saint.text: To sing is to pray twice.

entries.question: Is there a 'song of praise' in your heart today, or only a list of complaints?

saint.text: The soul's salvation is the only thing that matters.

entries.question: Is there a specific 'gate' of your heart that you have kept locked because you fear Christ's light?

saint.text: A martyr's blood is the seed of the Church.

entries.question: Are you willing to 'suffer' small social inconveniences for the sake of the 'Light of Life'?

saint.text: Faith is the light that guides us through the darkness of this world.

entries.question: Do you treat your coworkers and employees with the 'justice' that you would want from God?

saint.text: The more we give to God, the more He gives to us.

entries.question: Where is your 'own prudence' causing you anxiety because you haven't yet trusted the Lord with the outcome?

saint.text: Mary is the source of all our hope.
saint.who: Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal

entries.question: Do you pray with the confidence that God is actively 'listening' to you right now?

saint.text: Patience is the only way to conquer the world.

entries.question: What 'spiritual debris' has built up in your heart this month that needs to be cleared out?

saint.text: Let us always be prepared to meet the Lord.

entries.question: If Christ came for your soul tonight, would you be 'ready' or would you be ashamed of how you spent today?

saint.text: To follow Christ is the only path to true joy.

entries.question: As November ends, who in your life is waiting for you to 'cast a net' of faith and invite them to Christ?

saint.text: Advent is a time of waiting for the Light to enter our darkness.

entries.question: In the 'darkness' of your current struggles, are you looking for a worldly solution or for the 'Rain' of the Just One?

saint.text: A soul that is at peace with God is a soul that is ready for anything.

entries.question: Is your heart 'at peace' today, or are you letting the 'iniquity' of the world disturb your internal silence?

saint.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his own soul?
saint.work: Letters to the Society of Jesus

entries.question: Are you more concerned with 'gaining the world' (status and wealth) or with the health of your soul?

saint.text: The Son of God became man so that we might become God.

entries.question: Does the reality of 'God with us' (Emmanuel) change the way you face loneliness today?

saint.text: Prayer is the best preparation for the coming of the King.

entries.question: Are you using this season to 'prepare' your heart, or are you just busy with the 'preparations' of the world?

saint.text: The giver of every good gift is the Lord Himself.

entries.question: When you give to others today, are you doing it to be seen, or to reflect the 'secret' generosity of God?

saint.text: The Church is the ship in which we sail safely through the storms of life.

entries.question: Is there a 'storm' in your life right now where you have forgotten that Christ is the Captain of the ship?

saint.text: Mary is the most beautiful flower that has ever bloomed in the garden of God.

entries.question: How can you honor the 'purity' of Mary today in your own thoughts and conversations?

saint.text: Am I not here, who am your Mother? Are you not under my shadow and protection?
saint.who: St. Juan Diego (Words of Our Lady)

entries.question: Do you feel 'under the shadow' of Mary's protection, or are you trying to solve your problems entirely on your own?

saint.text: Our Lady of Loreto is the house where the Word became Flesh.

entries.question: Is your home a place where the 'Word' can dwell, or is it filled with the noise of distraction?

saint.text: The shepherd of the Church must be a defender of the faith.

entries.question: Are you 'defending' your faith in your social circles, or are you hiding it to fit in?

saint.text: I am the Mother of the true God for Whom one lives.

entries.question: Do you live as if you are truly 'living for God,' or are you just surviving for yourself?

saint.text: To die for the faith is to find the true light.

entries.question: Is there a 'darkness' in your life (envy, pride, or fear) that you have not yet allowed the Light of Christ to enter?

saint.text: In the evening of life, we will be judged on love alone.

entries.question: If you were 'judged on love' today, would you be satisfied with the way you treated the people closest to you?

saint.text: Silence is the guardian of the spiritual life.

entries.question: Can you find ten minutes of 'silence' today to simply listen for the Shepherd's voice?

saint.text: Every soul that loves is a soul that prays.

entries.question: Is your prayer life 'going forwards,' or have you stopped growing in your relationship with God?

saint.text: The wisdom of the world is a heavy burden, but the wisdom of God is a light yoke.

entries.question: Are you seeking 'prudence' (the right way to act) through prayer, or through the opinions of the world?

saint.text: Let us prepare the way of the Lord in our souls.

entries.question: What ' Bethlehem'—small, humble, and overlooked—is God using to work a miracle in your life right now?

saint.text: The heart of a Christian should be a dwelling place for God.

entries.question: If Christ were to be born in your 'heart' tonight, would He find it 'clean' and ready for Him?

saint.text: Mary's 'Yes' is the key that opened the door to our salvation.

entries.question: In what specific area of your life is God waiting for your 'Yes'—your total surrender?

saint.text: Blessed is the one who believes in the promises of the Lord.

entries.question: Do you 'believe' God's promises even when your current situation seems to contradict them?

saint.text: True joy is not found in things, but in the presence of God.

entries.question: Is your soul 'magnifying' (making bigger) the goodness of God today, or the problems you are facing?

saint.text: Silence is the language of God; all else is a poor translation.

entries.question: Are you 'preparing the way' for Christ in your home, or are you too busy with the noise of the holidays?

saint.text: Tonight, Heaven and Earth are joined in the Person of a Child.

entries.question: As you stand at the threshold of Christmas, what is the one 'gift' of your heart you want to give to the Christ Child?

saint.text: Awake, O man! For your sake God became man.

entries.question: How does the fact that 'God became man' change the way you see the dignity of every person you meet today?

saint.text: The first martyr is the seed of the Church's courage.

entries.question: Are you 'looking up' toward Heaven when you are faced with criticism, or are you looking for an earthly defense?

saint.text: God is love, and he that abideth in love, abideth in God.

entries.question: Is the 'love' you show others today a reflection of the 'Love' that is God?

saint.text: The innocent suffer, but their blood is not shed in vain.

entries.question: How are you protecting the 'innocence' of your own soul and the souls of the children in your life?

saint.text: I die for the Name of Jesus and for the defense of the Church.

entries.question: Are you 'edifying' your community, or are your words contributing to its division?

saint.text: Let us always be ready to serve the Lord with all our hearts.

entries.question: As the year draws to a close, can you see how God's 'eyes' have been upon you through every trial?

saint.text: The time of life is short; let us use it for the glory of God.

entries.question: As you stand at the end of this year, are you ready to meet the Son of Man today?
